description: Probes the AAS realisation of the DPP: IDTA 02099-1 DppMetadata idShorts, semanticIds, cardinalities, granularity mapping and versions, and the IDTA 02035 Digital Battery Passport parts, semanticIds and value lists.

items.question: In the IDTA 02099-1 DppMetadata submodel, are facilityId and contentSpecificationIds mandatory? How many of its top-level elements are mandatory?
items.expected_answer: No. facilityId and contentSpecificationIds are both optional with cardinality 0..1. The other seven (digitalProductPassportId, uniqueProductIdentifier, granularity, dppSchemaVersion, dppStatus, lastUpdate, economicOperatorId) have cardinality 1, so 7 are mandatory.

items.expected_answer: idShort lastUpdate, semanticId https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/lastUpdate/1, valueType xs:dateTime (cardinality 1), with supplementalSemanticId https://admin-shell.io/aas/3/2/AdministrativeInformation/updatedAt.

items.question: How does the DppMetadata granularity value map to the AAS AssetKind? In particular, what AssetKind corresponds to granularity 'Item' and to 'Model'?
items.expected_answer: Item maps to AssetKind Instance, Model maps to Type, and Batch maps to Batch (supplementalSemanticIds https://admin-shell.io/aas/3/2/AssetKind/...). Role and NotApplicable have no ESPR equivalent.

items.question: Is an AAS that contains the seven IDTA 02035 battery submodels already the Digital Product Passport required by EN 18223?
items.expected_answer: No. Per IDTA 02099-1 an AAS is not, by itself, the DPP; a DPP can be derived from it when the AAS contains the submodels with the required data points plus the DppMetadata submodel.

items.question: Which AAS serialization does the EN 18223 DPP metadata payload map to when built from the DppMetadata submodel?
items.expected_answer: The Value-Only format of the DppMetadata submodel; for DPP metadata there is exactly one correct serialization.

items.expected_answer: IDTA 02099-1 recommends the semanticId of each Submodel Template Specification belonging to the DPP; if several regulations apply, all their semanticIds are added to the one DPP.

items.question: What are the allowed LifeCycleStage values in the IDTA 02035-1 BatteryNameplate, and what must happen when a battery is remanufactured or repurposed and placed on the market again?
items.expected_answer: 'original', 'repurposed', 're-used', 'remanufactured' or 'waste' (IRDIs 0173-1#07-ACC020#001 to ACC024#001). A new battery passport must be issued when the battery is remanufactured, repurposed or prepared for re-use/repurpose and placed on the market again.

items.question: IDTA 02099-1 section 2.1 says the battery passport submodels were based on 'DIN DKE SPEC 91100'. Which DIN DKE SPEC do the IDTA 02035 parts actually reference?
items.expected_answer: DIN DKE SPEC 99100; the 02035 parts cite '99100 chapter reference' for their elements, so '91100' in 02099-1 is a typo.

items.question: Is there any IDTA submodel template for expressing data retention policies in an AAS, or must retention always be handled outside the AAS?
items.expected_answer: Yes: IDTA 02056 Data Retention Policies (v1.0, June 2024) represents retention policies applied to AAS elements via semantic identifiers, including how long data must be stored before deletion and an audit log. It does not by itself set a legal DPP retention period.

citation.quote: A data retention policy defines how long data must be stored before it may be deleted.

items.question: Are all seven IDTA 02035 Digital Battery Passport parts still at version 1.0 of 18.02.2026? What is the latest published version of Part 5 Product Condition?
items.expected_answer: No. Part 5 Product Condition is at version 1.0.2 (August 2026), after a 1.0.1 bugfix release in April 2026; other parts also have 1.0.1 bugfix releases (e.g. Parts 4, 6 and 7, May 2026).
